items.title: Pauline Hanson's criticism of Guardian reporter labelled an 'assault on free press'
items.description: Pauline Hanson's public excoriation of a Guardian journalist questioning her at the National Press Club yesterday is an "assault on the freedom of the press", the media union says, as Labor and Liberal MPs criticise the One Nation leader for getting personal with journalists.

items.title: Hanson's fiery address creates risk for One Nation
items.description: In one press club appearance, we've learned more about where Hanson stands. And that creates risk for One Nation.

items.title: Couple left with nothing after investing $1m in 7-Eleven franchise
items.description: Jotika and Sunny Sharma took out a loan to purchase their Sydney franchise in 2015. When the lease expired this year, their relationship with the convenience store giant turned ugly.

items.title: US releases text of ceasefire deal struck with Iran
items.description: The official text of the memorandum of understanding includes American commitments to remove sanctions imposed on Tehran while Iran will agree to dilute its enriched uranium stockpile.

items.title: Electricity like milk? The plan to simplify complex power bills
items.description: Millions of Australians have been often unwittingly moved to complex and variable power tariffs. An energy watchdog says bills must be simplified.

items.title: KPMG the latest example of accountants being unaccountable
items.description: Bean counters have historically been viewed as dull, dull, dull. But since the turn of the century, accounting scandals have come thick and fast in Australia.

items.title: Live: England takes on Croatia after DR Congo holds Portugal to draw
items.description: England kicks off its campaign against Croatia, the team that beat the Three Lions at the semifinal stage in 2018, after Ronaldo stumbles as Portugal drew with DR Congo. Follow live.

items.title: HSBC fought customers 'tooth and nail' over scam but now it's fronting court
items.description: HSBC customers who became victims of a long-running "spoofing" scam hope the bank will take full responsibility for its "system failures" in Federal Court this week.

items.title: Don't expect a post-budget $1,250 boost this tax time
items.description: There was a lot of talk about the $1,000 instant tax reduction and the $250 Working Australians Tax Offset in the federal budget. But they won't be in play at tax time this year.

items.title: There's blood in Blue water after NSW collapse in Origin II
items.description: New South Wales travelled to the MCG with the Origin series within their grasp but after the disaster that ensued success has never felt further away.

items.title: Uni students tackle 'character-building' remote living through placements
items.description: University student Tarhnee says her survival kit for a nursing prac placement was food, a swag, a chair and a little table for her laptop.

items.title: Sydney-to-London unveiled as first route for Qantas's Project Sunrise
items.description: The flights, set to begin take off from next year, will mark the first time flights from the east coast will complete the Kangaroo Route without a stop over.

items.title: Wife and carer 'dumbfounded' by husband's aged care assessment
items.description: Melbourne man Graham Crossan relies on his wife Gaynor to help him eat, move and even breathe. But a new assessment tool means he's been refused funding for more support.

items.title: Mangione to argue he suffered 'extreme emotional disturbance' in murder trial
items.description: The 28-year-old is accused of killing an American health insurance executive. If successful, his defence could see him convicted of manslaughter rather than murder.

items.title: Australian horror film Leviticus weaponises homophobia to terrifying effect
items.description: Writer and director Adrian Chiarella's debut supernatural horror feature, Leviticus, is as romantic as it is scary.

items.title: Manuel is on a mission to end illegal gold mining in the Amazon
items.description: In Peru, I meet a man risking his life to end illegal gold mining in the Amazon, in the hope of saving his beloved town before it's too late.

items.title: Quiz: Grab your suitcase, we're going on a trip
items.description: Which airport hosts the world's largest indoor waterfall? What is the Swiss delicacy raclette?

items.title: Perry stars in big win over Bangladesh
items.description: Ellyse Perry has starred with bat and ball as Australia gave their net run-rate a massive boost with a landslide win over Bangladesh at Headingley in the T20 World Cup.

items.title: Debutant stars for Australia in T20 win over Bangladesh
items.description: Cooper Connolly and the Aussie spinners have guided Australia to a T20 win over Bangladesh with 10 balls to spare.

items.title: Father of 17yo killed in e-bike crash speaks after teen driver sentenced
items.description: A Gold Coast father whose son died in an electric bike crash has spoken out after the driver was sentenced, saying the devices need better regulation.

items.title: AI factory 'brings into doubt' future of Tasmania's Marinus Link
items.description: Tasmania's cool climate and access to renewable energy has made it an attractive place for AI data centre investment, but energy industry voices are warning that the business case for the Marinus Link project appears increasingly unviable if power-hungry players such as AI data centres continue to expand across the state.

items.title: RBA warns financial industry to prepare for 'more shock-prone future'
items.description: A new era of strategic uncertainty has serious implications for Australia's financial industry, the Reserve Bank warns.

items.title: 'Whole bloodlines' have been lost in Sudan but the world isn't watching
items.description: Sudanese Australians are kept up at night thinking of family and friends trapped as a result of one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

items.title: Bill restricting late-term abortions fails to pass SA lower house
items.description: South Australia's lower house has voted against a bill to restrict access to abortions past 25 weeks. The legislation was defeated 36 votes to 9.

items.title: Cambodia says 310,000 suspected scammers left country amid crackdown
items.description: A report by Amnesty International casts doubt on the impact of Cambodia's high-profile scam industry crackdown, finding authorities failed to dismantle the "vast majority" of operations.
